info.title: FactLot
info.description: The open fact layer for commercial real estate AI agents: deterministic CRE calculators with audit trails, canonical FactLot IDs, and cited-fact validation. Call these operations instead of doing lease, CAM, rent, loan, or return math yourself.

post.description: Build a base-rent schedule from commencement date, term, area, starting $/SF/yr, escalations (percent or fixed $/SF), and abated months. Lease months run from the commencement day-of-month with no calendar proration (warns when commencement is mid-month). Returns rent steps, totals, expiration date, and a calculation trace. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.rent_schedule@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Compute effective rent, straight-line net effective rent, and discounted net effective rent ($/SF/yr) after free rent, TI allowance, leasing commissions, and other landlord concessions. Rent is monthly in advance from the commencement day (no calendar proration), discounted at annual rate ÷ 12. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.net_effective_rent@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

schedule.description: The lease's base-rent terms (same input as calc_rent_schedule).

ti_allowance_psf.description: Landlord-funded tenant improvement allowance, USD per SF, paid once at commencement (not per year).

leasing_commissions.description: Total leasing commissions paid by landlord, USD.

other_concessions.description: Any other landlord concessions paid at commencement (moving allowance, buyout), USD.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08 (monthly rate = annual ÷ 12); 0 gives the undiscounted (straight-line) NER.

post.description: Rank 2–20 lease proposals with different terms, sizes, free rent, TI, concessions, and operating-expense structures (gross, NNN, base year, expense stop, with opex growth) on one discounted $/SF/yr basis, per rentable or usable SF (load factor): effective occupancy cost (tenant perspective) or discounted net effective rent after landlord-borne opex and optional pre-commencement downtime (landlord perspective). Cash flows monthly in advance at annual rate ÷ 12; warns when the usable-SF ranking differs and when terms differ. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.compare_proposals@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

perspective.description: Whose economics to rank on: tenant (effective occupancy cost, lower is better) or landlord (discounted net effective rent, higher is better).

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08, applied to every proposal (monthly rate = annual ÷ 12, cash flows at the start of each month).

area_basis.description: Area the $/SF/yr metric is divided by: rentable (schedule.area_sf, the default) or usable (each proposal's usable_sf, or area_sf ÷ load_factor). Rents and expenses stay quoted per rentable SF; use usable when proposals have different load factors and the tenant needs a fixed usable area.

name.description: Unique label for the proposal, e.g. building name.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

schedule.description: Base-rent terms of this proposal (same input as calc_rent_schedule); schedule.area_sf is the rentable area.

usable_sf.description: Usable square feet of this proposal (at most schedule.area_sf). Give this or load_factor, not both; required for area_basis usable.

load_factor.description: Rentable ÷ usable area, e.g. 1.15 (usable_sf = area_sf ÷ load_factor). Give this or usable_sf, not both.

ti_allowance_psf.description: TI allowance paid by the landlord, USD per rentable SF, once at commencement (not per year).

other_concessions.description: Other cash concessions to the tenant at commencement (moving allowance, buyout), USD.

leasing_commissions.description: Leasing commissions paid by landlord at commencement, USD (landlord perspective only).

operating_expenses.description: Operating-expense structure of this proposal: gross, nnn, base_year, or expense_stop, with a lease-year-1 estimate and growth. Tenant perspective adds what the tenant pays; landlord perspective deducts what the landlord bears. Omit to price no operating expenses (as before).

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses the landlord pays, $/SF/yr in lease year 1 (used in the landlord perspective; the tenant pays none).

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Full-service gross: the landlord pays all operating expenses; the tenant pays none beyond base rent.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Net (NNN): the tenant pays all operating expenses, estimated at expense_psf_annual in lease year 1.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

base_year_psf_annual.description: Base-year operating expenses, $/SF/yr. Defaults to expense_psf_annual (the base year is lease year 1).

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Gross with a base year: the tenant pays operating expenses above the base-year amount.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

stop_psf_annual.description: Expense stop, $/SF/yr: the tenant pays operating expenses above this fixed amount.

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Gross with an expense stop: the tenant pays operating expenses above a fixed $/SF/yr stop.

additional_costs_psf_annual.description: Other costs the tenant pays on top of base rent, flat $/SF/yr on rentable area (tenant perspective only), e.g. parking. Prefer operating_expenses for opex pass-throughs, which can grow and follow a base year or stop.

tenant_upfront_costs.description: Tenant's own costs at commencement not covered by allowances (TI overage, moving), USD.

downtime_months.description: Landlord perspective: vacant months before this proposal commences (no rent; the landlord carries lease-year-1 operating expenses if operating_expenses is given). The metric is then the level monthly amount over downtime plus term. Ignored for the tenant.

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Percentage (overage) rent for a lease year: net sales after exclusions over a natural or fixed breakpoint, prorated for partial years, less amounts already paid. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.percentage_rent@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

gross_sales.description: Gross sales reported for the lease year (or partial year), USD.

sales_exclusions.description: Sales excluded by the lease (returns, sales tax, gift cards, employee sales, …), USD.

base_rent_annual.description: Annual base rent, USD per year (a full lease year, even for a partial period); used for the natural breakpoint.

breakpoint.description: Breakpoint above which percentage rent applies. Default: natural.

oneOf.description: Natural breakpoint = annual base rent ÷ rate.

amount.description: Annual sales breakpoint stated in the lease, USD.

oneOf.description: Artificial (fixed) breakpoint stated in the lease.

period_fraction.description: Fraction of a full lease year covered (e.g. 0.5 for a six-month partial year). Prorates the breakpoint.

percentage_rent_paid.description: Percentage rent already paid during the period, USD.

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Reconcile a tenant's annual CAM charge: exclusions, occupancy gross-up of variable expenses, pro rata share, controllable-expense caps (compounding_from_base, simple_from_base, year_over_year), an admin fee (before or after the cap, inside or outside it, with per-line exclusions), base year or expense stop, partial-year occupancy (move-in/move-out prorates share, cap, and base by days), and estimates paid. Returns balance due and a full trace with order-of-operations warnings. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.cam_reconciliation@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

year.description: Calendar or lease year being reconciled.

category.description: Expense line as named in the operating statement, e.g. "janitorial".

amount.description: Building-level actual expense for the year, USD.

controllable.description: Subject to the cap. Taxes, insurance, and utilities are typically uncontrollable.

recoverable.description: Excluded expenses (capital items, landlord-only costs) are dropped entirely.

variable.description: Varies with occupancy, so eligible for gross-up (janitorial, utilities, management fee).

admin_fee_applies.description: Included in the admin_fee base. Set false for lines the lease excludes from the fee (often taxes, insurance, utilities, or a management fee already charged).

expenses.description: Building operating expense lines for the year.

gross_up.description: Gross up variable expenses to the target occupancy when actual occupancy is lower. Omit if the lease has no gross-up.

actual_occupancy.description: Average occupancy for the year, e.g. 0.82.

target_occupancy.description: Gross-up occupancy stated in the lease (commonly 0.95 or 1.0).

structure.description: Expense structure from the lease. Default: net.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its full share of recoverable expenses (NNN / net).

base_year_expenses.description: Total building recoverable expenses in the base year, already grossed up, USD.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over base-year expenses.

stop_amount.description: Building-level expense stop, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over a fixed expense stop.

cap.description: Cap on the tenant's share of controllable expenses. Omit if the lease has no cap.

method.description: compounding_from_base: reference × (1+rate)^years (often called cumulative, compounding). simple_from_base: reference × (1 + rate × years) (cumulative, non-compounding). year_over_year: prior year's capped amount × (1+rate) (non-cumulative). Map the lease language to one of these explicitly.

rate.description: Annual cap as a decimal, e.g. 0.05.

reference_amount.description: Tenant's share of controllable expenses in the reference year: the base year for *_from_base, or the prior year's capped amount for year_over_year, USD.

years_elapsed.description: Years since the base year (required for `*_from_base`).

admin_fee.description: Administrative fee the lease adds to the tenant's share. Omit if the lease has none.

rate.description: Administrative or management fee as a decimal of the fee base, e.g. 0.15 for 15%. The base is the tenant's share of recoverable lines with admin_fee_applies (after gross-up).

applied.description: Fee on controllable lines computed on the tenant's share before the cap (before_cap) or on the capped amount (after_cap). Fees on uncontrollable lines are never capped. Irrelevant without a cap.

capped.description: True when the fee on controllable lines counts toward the controllable cap (controllable share plus fee may not exceed the cap limit); false adds it outside the cap.

occupancy.description: Partial-year occupancy: the tenant's share, cap limit, and base-year or stop deduction are prorated by occupied days ÷ period days (both inclusive), so a full-year cap and base are not applied to a part year. Omit for a full year.

move_in_date.description: Date the tenant's share starts within the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_start_date.

move_out_date.description: Last day of the tenant's share within the period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_end_date.

period_start_date.description: First day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to January 1 of year; set it for a lease year.

period_end_date.description: Last day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days after the start). Defaults to December 31 of year.

estimates_paid.description: Estimated CAM payments the tenant made during the year, USD (total for the year, not monthly).

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Size the maximum loan under any combination of max LTV, min DSCR, and min debt yield for a given NOI, rate, and amortization. Reports the binding constraint, debt service, and resulting metrics; optionally a stress table over NOI, rate, and value shocks (max loan, binding constraint, LTV, DSCR, debt yield per scenario) and the refinance shortfall against an existing loan balance. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.debt_sizing@3 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

value.description: Appraised or underwritten value, USD. Required when max_ltv is set.

min_dscr.description: Minimum debt service coverage ratio, e.g. 1.25.

round_down_to.description: Round the final loan amount down to this increment (lenders often use 1,000 or 10,000).

existing_loan_balance.description: Balance of the loan being refinanced, USD. Adds a refinance result (shortfall or excess proceeds against the max loan) and a shortfall per stress scenario.

stress.description: Stress table: every combination of the NOI, rate, and value shocks (up to 1,000 scenarios), each sized under the same constraints and rounding. The base result is unchanged.

noi_shocks.description: Relative NOI changes as decimals, e.g. [-0.05, -0.1, -0.2] for NOI down 5%, 10%, 20%. Omit for no NOI shock.

rate_shocks.description: Absolute changes to rate_annual as decimals, e.g. [0.005, 0.01] for +50 and +100 bp. The stressed rate must stay at or above 0 and below 1. Omit for no rate shock.

value_shocks.description: Relative value changes as decimals, e.g. [-0.1, -0.2]; requires value. Omit for no value shock.

value_moves_with_noi.description: Also scale value by each NOI shock (value × (1 + noi_shock), a constant cap rate), as a lender repricing value on stressed NOI would.

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Remeasure a lessee's lease liability and right-of-use asset under ASC 842 after a modification, lease-term reassessment, contingency resolution, or residual value guarantee change: new liability (PV of remaining payments), liability and ROU adjustments with any gain (ASC 842-20-35-4), and the per-period amortization table (operating: straight-line single lease cost; finance: interest plus amortization) in cents that foots: every row rolls forward exactly, totals are the row sums, and the final period trues up liability and ROU asset to zero. Warns where judgment is needed. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.lease_remeasurement_asc842@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

classification.description: Lessee classification (ASC 842-10-25-2): operating (single straight-line lease cost) or finance (interest on the liability plus straight-line ROU amortization).

period.description: Period index counted from the remeasurement date (1 = first remaining period).

amount.description: Lease payment due in that period after the event, USD for the period (a monthly amount when periods_per_year is 12, not annualized): fixed and in-substance fixed payments, less incentives receivable (ASC 842-10-30-5).

payments.description: Remaining lease payments after the event, in ascending period order. Periods not listed carry no payment (rent-free).

remaining_periods.description: Remaining lease term in periods after the event. Defaults to the last period index in payments; set it higher when the final periods are rent-free.

payment_timing.description: Whether each payment falls at the beginning (in advance) or end (in arrears) of its period.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate applied to the remaining payments, e.g. 0.06. Nominal: the periodic rate is this ÷ periods_per_year.

periods_per_year.description: Payment periods per year (12 for monthly, 4 for quarterly).

discount_rate_updated.description: True when discount_rate_annual was determined at the remeasurement date (ASC 842-10-35-5: required for modifications and lease-term or purchase-option reassessments); false when it is the rate from commencement (kept for contingency resolutions and residual value guarantee changes).

liability_before.description: Carrying amount of the lease liability immediately before the remeasurement, USD.

rou_asset_before.description: Carrying amount of the right-of-use asset immediately before the remeasurement, USD (after any impairment).

event.description: What triggered the remeasurement: modification_extend_term / modification_shorten_term / modification_change_in_payments (a modification not accounted for as a separate contract, ASC 842-10-25-8 and 25-11), reassessment_of_term_or_option (ASC 842-10-35-1 and 35-4(c)), contingency_resolved (variable payments became fixed, ASC 842-10-35-4(b)), residual_value_guarantee_change (ASC 842-10-35-4(c)(3)), or index_or_rate_change (ASC 842-10-35-4: not a remeasurement trigger by itself; computed as if remeasured for another reason).

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Prepayment premium, total payoff, and cost as a share of balance for a fixed-rate amortizing or interest-only loan under yield maintenance (PV of remaining payments or rate differential, with a minimum and an explicit discounting convention), a step-down schedule, a flat percentage, or defeasance (cost of the securities portfolio that funds the remaining payments plus stated costs). Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.prepayment_and_defeasance@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

balance.description: Outstanding principal balance at the payoff date, USD.

remaining_term_months.description: Months from the payoff date to the loan's maturity date (the balloon is due with the final payment).

amortization_months.description: Remaining amortization basis in months at the payoff date (e.g. 300 for a 30-year schedule with 5 years elapsed); 0 for interest-only. Must be at least remaining_term_months.

accrued_interest.description: Accrued but unpaid interest to the payoff date, USD; added to the total payoff.

treasury_rate_annual.description: Yield on the reference Treasury (usually the one maturing closest to the loan's maturity), e.g. 0.041.

spread_annual.description: Spread added to the Treasury yield for discounting, e.g. 0.005 when the note says 'Treasury plus 50 basis points'. Default 0 (Treasury flat).

minimum_pct.description: Minimum premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.01 for a 1% floor (default). 0 for no floor.

basis.description: pv_of_payments (default): premium = PV of the remaining scheduled payments at the discount rate − balance. rate_differential: premium = PV of (note rate − discount rate) ÷ 12 × scheduled balance for each remaining month.

discount_convention.description: Compounding convention for the discount rate. monthly (default): monthly rate = annual ÷ 12. semiannual: annual is a bond-equivalent yield, monthly rate = (1 + annual ÷ 2)^(1/6) − 1. Lenders differ; read the note.

oneOf.description: Yield maintenance.

loan_month.description: Loan month (1 = first month after origination) in which the payoff occurs.

through_month.description: Last loan month in which this percentage applies.

pct.description: Premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.05 for 5%.

schedule.description: Step-down schedule in ascending through_month order, e.g. 5-4-3-2-1. After the last through_month the loan is open (0%).

oneOf.description: Step-down (declining percentage) premium.

pct.description: Premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.02.

oneOf.description: Flat percentage premium.

anyOf.description: One flat annual yield for all replacement securities.

months.description: Months from the payoff date up to and including which this yield applies; points in ascending order.

rate.description: Annual yield on replacement securities maturing at or before that month, e.g. 0.042.

anyOf.description: Yield curve as a step function: each payment uses the first point whose months ≥ its month; beyond the last point, the last rate.

replacement_yield.description: Yield on the government securities bought to fund the remaining payments: a flat annual rate, or a list of {months, rate} points.

costs.description: Stated transaction costs, USD: defeasance consultant, legal, accountant, rating agency, servicer and custodian fees.

discount_convention.description: Compounding convention for the discount rate. monthly (default): monthly rate = annual ÷ 12. semiannual: annual is a bond-equivalent yield, monthly rate = (1 + annual ÷ 2)^(1/6) − 1. Lenders differ; read the note.

oneOf.description: Defeasance: buy securities that replicate the remaining payments.

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Weighted average remaining lease term in years as of a date (actual days ÷ 365.25), weighted by each lease's area_sf (weight_by "area") or annual_rent (weight_by "rent"). Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.walt@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

as_of.description: Date to measure remaining term from, YYYY-MM-DD.

weight_by.description: How each lease is weighted: "area" uses its area_sf, "rent" its annual_rent (that field is then required on every lease). Default "area".

id.description: Your identifier for the lease (ideally a FactLot lease ID).

area_sf.description: Leased square feet (required when weight_by is area).

annual_rent.description: Current annual rent, USD per year (required when weight_by is rent).

leases.description: Leases in the portfolio or building.

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: NPV of periodic cash flows (t = 0, 1, 2, ...; the t = 0 flow is not discounted) at a per-period discount rate given as a decimal. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.npv@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

cash_flows.description: Periodic cash flows at t = 0, 1, 2, …; negative for outflows (e.g. purchase price at t = 0). At most 10000.

rate.description: Discount rate per period as a decimal, e.g. 0.08 for 8%. Match the cash-flow period: for monthly flows pass the monthly rate (e.g. 0.06 ÷ 12 = 0.005).

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Periodic and annualized IRR of periodic cash flows, as decimals (0.085 = 8.5%), solved deterministically by scanning a 1-point grid of per-period rates and bisecting each sign change; reports every root it finds when cash flows have multiple IRRs (two roots within one grid step can be missed). Errors when the flows do not change sign or no root lies between -99.99% and 1000% per period. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.irr@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

cash_flows.description: Periodic cash flows at t = 0, 1, 2, …; negative for outflows (e.g. purchase price at t = 0). At most 1200.

periods_per_year.description: Cash-flow periods per year, used only to annualize the result: 1 for annual flows, 4 for quarterly, 12 for monthly.

200.description: Result: { value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance }.

400.description: Invalid input; read `issues`, fix the arguments, and retry.

post.description: Compare leasing with buying over a fixed horizon: NPV of each case's annual cash costs (rent, free rent, tenant expenses, and move-in costs versus equity, debt service, owner expenses, reserves, and a sale at the horizon by stated value or exit cap rate), optionally after tax, with the year-by-year tables and the break-even residual value at which owning equals leasing. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.lease_vs_own@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

horizon_years.description: Analysis horizon in years. Both cases are compared over this period; the own case sells at the end of it.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08, applied to both cases' year-end cash flows (year 0 = closing / move-in).

annual_rent.description: Rent due in each year of the horizon, USD, year 1 first. Must have exactly horizon_years entries.

oneOf.description: Explicit rent per year.

escalation_rate_annual.description: Compounding annual bump, e.g. 0.03: rent_k = base × (1 + e)^(k − 1).

oneOf.description: Base rent with a compounding annual escalation.

rent.description: Annual rent, as an explicit schedule or base rent with escalation.

post.description: Check one FactLot fact against the published fact schema (spec/schemas/fact.json): subject URN, dotted predicate, as_of date, provenance, optional rights; unknown fields are rejected at every level. Rules: every fact except a computed one cites at least one source (an inferred fact cites the evidence it was inferred from); a computed fact names its formula or cites a source; valid_from is not after valid_to; a source span does not end before it starts. For Ingest predicates (lease.expiration_date, lease.rentable_area_sf, lease.base_rent_schedule, ...) the value must have the predicate's shape and every source quote must state the value, by the same written-form rules as doc_verify_facts (a quote saying "2,500 square feet" does not support 1000). Not checked: that the quote is in the document, that the document or sha256 exists, that supersedes IDs exist, and quotes for other predicates; doc_verify_facts with the document's pages checks the quote. Returns { valid, issues }. Call before storing or sharing facts.

post.description: Check values YOU extracted from a document against its text, deterministically; FactLot runs no model. Send the pages as text and one candidate per value: {predicate, value, quote, page}. Each candidate is checked in order: (1) the value's shape (Ingest predicates such as lease.expiration_date YYYY-MM-DD, lease.pro_rata_share in (0, 1], ordered lease.base_rent_schedule steps; any other dotted predicate needs a non-empty value); (2) the quote, at least 12 characters, is on the cited page, where only whitespace, line breaks, letter case and typographic quotes and dashes may differ (a word hyphenated across a line must keep its hyphen; a quote found on exactly one other page is accepted with the page corrected); (3) every number, date and party name in the value is written in the quote, in any common form: 1250000 matches "$1,250,000.00", 0.03 matches "3%" or "three percent", 2031-06-30 matches "June 30, 2031" or "6/30/2031"; (4) a confidence you give below 0.8 holds it for review. Returns verified (FactLot facts: method extracted, citing document_id, page, quote and character span, plus which value parts were and were not checked), needs_review (the quote is on the page but does not state the value, or low confidence) and rejected (wrong shape; quote missing, too short, or on several pages), each with a reason to act on. Not checked: enums and free-text summaries, meaning (a quote stating the number in another context passes), and whether the pages came from the file whose sha256 you give.

When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

post.description: Current-state lease abstract from a lease and its amendments, with amendment precedence. Give each document's pages with the candidates you extracted (checked exactly as doc_verify_facts checks them), or the facts doc_verify_facts already returned for it (without pages only the value against its quote is rechecked, marked quote_on_page: false). The original applies first, then amendments by effective_date (in the order given if any is undated); a later document's value for a predicate controls, and the earlier one moves to history and is linked through supersedes. Each field gives its value, the controlling document, page, quote and fact, the superseded history, conflicts (one document stating two different values) and open_items (a candidate for that predicate in the controlling or a later document that needs review or was rejected, so the value may not be final). FactLot only orders what you extracted: it does not find terms you missed, and an amendment that changes a term without restating it ("extended by 24 months") needs the resulting value extracted with that sentence as its quote, which the quote check will hold for review if the date is not written there.

post.summary: Compare asserted values with a lease
post.description: Compare values another document asserts (an estoppel, rent roll or offering memo, mapped by you to predicates) with verified lease facts from doc_abstract_lease or doc_verify_facts. Each asserted value comes back match, mismatch (with the differing fields), not_in_lease, or ambiguous_in_lease (two current lease facts disagree), with the controlling lease citation (document, page, quote). Values compare exactly as JSON: numbers by value, strings exactly (a name written differently is a mismatch), and for an object only the fields you assert. Facts another fact supersedes are ignored. The lease facts must pass fact_validate; FactLot does not re-read the lease, so pass the facts its document tools returned.

post.summary: Verify a claim against a document
post.description: Check one claim against a document page: {predicate, value} (anything doc_verify_facts accepts) or a short claim sentence, plus the verbatim quote and page it rests on. Returns supported (the quote is on the page and every checked number, date and name in the claim is written in it), contradicted (the quote is on the page and states other numbers or dates of the same kind, listed in quote_states), or unverifiable (the quote is not on the page, nothing in the claim can be checked, or the quote states no value of that kind), with the evidence (document_id, page, quote, span) and each part checked. Textual, not semantic: for a sentence only its numbers and dates are compared, never its meaning, and a quote that mentions the right number for a different term still supports it.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).
